items.item: Default argument values are evaluated once at def time: a mutable default (list/dict) is shared across calls; use None and create inside
Keyword-only (*) and positional-only (/) parameters to make pipeline function signatures explicit and safe to evolve
Closures bind late: lambdas/inner functions created in a loop see the variable's final value; bind via default arg or functools.partial
Dataclasses for record/config types: frozen=True, slots=True, kw_only, field(default_factory=...) instead of mutable defaults
Class contract recall: defining __eq__ without __hash__ makes instances unhashable; hash must be consistent with eq and stable for objects used as dict/set keys

items.item: Comprehensions have their own scope (loop var does not leak); list vs set vs dict vs generator expression; pass a generator expression to sum/any/max/join to avoid materializing; 3.15 adds unpacking in comprehensions ([*xs for xs in batches], PEP 798)
The with statement guarantees __exit__ runs on normal exit, exception, return or break; __exit__ returning a truthy value suppresses the exception
@contextmanager: put cleanup in try/finally around the yield, or it is skipped when the body raises; yield exactly once
contextlib.ExitStack for a dynamic number of resources (open N partition files, roll back on partial failure); closing() and suppress() helpers
A generator holding a resource (open file/cursor) only runs its finally/with exit when exhausted or close()d (GeneratorExit); a partially consumed generator relies on GC

Decorators: @d def f is f = d(f); always functools.wraps the wrapper; decorator factories for arguments (e.g. @retry(times=3)); applied at import time; type them with ParamSpec, not Callable[..., Any]
functools.cache/lru_cache: unbounded cache grows forever, args must be hashable, and on methods it keeps self alive (memory leak)
Iterator protocol (__iter__/__next__/StopIteration); iterators and generators are single-pass: a second consumer silently gets nothing
Generator pipelines for bounded memory: chain generator functions (read -> parse -> filter -> batch -> write); yield from for delegation; work happens only when pulled
Generator laziness traps: argument validation and errors surface only at first next(); a StopIteration raised inside a generator becomes RuntimeError
itertools for streaming: islice, chain.from_iterable, batched(n, strict=) for chunked writes, groupby only groups consecutive keys (sort first), tee buffers unboundedly
Type hints are not enforced at runtime; modern syntax: list[int], dict[str, X], X | None (PEP 585/604), no typing.List/Optional needed
Annotate parameters with abstract collections.abc types (Iterable, Iterator, Mapping, Sequence) and return concrete types; type generator functions as Iterator[T]
Protocol for structural typing (e.g. 'anything with .write(bytes)') and TypedDict for JSON-shaped records; TypedDict is a plain dict at runtime
PEP 695 generics syntax: def first[T](xs: Iterable[T]) -> T and the type alias statement (3.12+)
3.14 deferred evaluation of annotations (PEP 649/749): forward references work without quotes or from __future__ import annotations; read them with annotationlib
Exception hygiene: catch narrowly, re-raise with raise ... from err (chaining), never bare except/pass; return/break/continue in finally is now a SyntaxWarning (PEP 765, 3.14)
Explicit encoding= on open(); 3.15 makes UTF-8 the default regardless of locale (PEP 686), plus newline='' for csv
